attributes.refutation_detail: The run-49 screen's DATA is correct and its CONCLUSION is not. It concluded 'the queue behind it is EMPTY in both directions that matter: ZERO NonMatching units sit in the 98.5%-99.99% matched-code band, and ZERO have all functions matched with code bytes short', and the atree wall record repeats it as 'there is no second candidate and no near-miss queue behind this one'. Both stated criteria are CODE-BYTE criteria, and neither can see a unit whose distance to a flip is one FUNCTION: game/mb/mb_camera is 76.63% matched code, game/world/newcam 93.91%, game/audio/dcsdrv 28.65% - all far outside a 98.5-99.99% band, and all ONE function from a flip. Code percent is dominated by function SIZE, so a TU whose single open function is large ranks as far from a flip as one with twenty open functions. THE REFUTATION IS NOT A HEAD-VS-c8a28c3bb ARTEFACT: `git diff --name-only c3f3aea99~1..HEAD` shows runs 48-49 touched only boss, critter, gamemain, player, mb_tree, movieplayer, dbgtext, pb_frame, psfx, cardutil, gauntworld and items - mb_camera, newcam, dcsdrv and sounds_evt are all absent, so all four stood at distance 1 when the screen ran and it missed them by method, not by age. CONSEQUENCE FOR DISPATCH: the run-49 conclusion that 'a FLIP lane has nothing to harvest' does not follow from its own evidence. The step-0-of-a-CLOSE-lane doctrine remains right, and this roster says which CLOSE lanes it pays for: a lane sent at mb_camera, newcam or dcsdrv is one function from a linked TU.

falsifier: Re-run the join and count `total_functions - matched_functions` per NonMatching unit. A run in which no NonMatching unit sits at distance 1 refutes this. Independently, per candidate: `python tools/gdl/nearmiss.py --min 0 --grep <unit>` returning more than one row for mb_camera, newcam or dcsdrv would mean the report totals and the per-function queue disagree, and the roster would have to be rebuilt from the latter.
